title: Production and Dev Hostname Family Separation

phases.objective: Define explicit Production and Dev hostname families for auth, MCP, and Activation, bind each family to its own deployment authority and credential namespace, and fail closed on unmatched or cross-environment routing.

e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The policy and local staging templates prove that Production hostnames route only to the Hostinger Production boundary, Dev hostnames route only to the opt-in local Tunnel origin, credentials are namespace-separated, and unmatched hostnames return a fail-closed 404 without DNS or provider mutation.
steps: Load the machine-readable domain family policy and validate the six explicit application hostnames.
Verify Production auth, MCP, and Activation entries use Hostinger Production and staging entries use the local app origin.
Verify the Production tunnel is disabled, the staging tunnel is opt-in, and the connector recovery hostname is excluded from both families.
Parse staging env and Compose without starting containers and reject Production hostnames or credentials in the staging template.
Run the bounded domain-family regression and emit only secret-free pass/fail evidence.
assertions: Production is exactly auth.mad4b.com, mcp.mad4b.com, and activation.mad4b.com; staging is exactly dev.mad4b.com, mcp_dev.mad4b.com, and activation_dev.mad4b.com.
No hostname belongs to both families and connector.mad4b.com remains independent.
Production and staging have distinct origin kinds, deployment providers, credential namespaces, and tunnel authority.
The local staging tunnel remains behind the explicit tunnel profile and targets only http://app:8080.
Unmatched hostnames fail closed with HTTP 404, and Auto Pilot performs no DNS, tunnel, Hostinger, database, migration, or provider mutation.
MIGRATION_APPLIED=false and DATABASE_MUTATED=false remain explicit local defaults.
Staging uses host-only Tenant GPT SSO cookies and never shares a .mad4b.com cookie with Production.

The current Activation Gateway bundle is Production-only for activation.mad4b.com to https://auth.mad4b.com; activation_dev.mad4b.com remains reserved-disabled until a dedicated staging bundle exists.
The Dev MCP hostname remains reserved-disabled until the explicit staging MCP runtime flag is enabled under separate credentials.
The staging hostname list in env is declaration-only; Cloudflare remote ingress is the source of truth, and any mismatch denies exposure without origin fallback.

phases.objective: Validate all six DNS records and live ingress mappings after authorized Cloudflare provisioning without allowing the local Auto Pilot to mutate provider state.
blockers: Cloudflare DNS records and tunnel ingress are provider-side resources and are not provisioned by this source change.
Live validation requires the operator's Windows host, a running local Compose stack, and a dedicated Dev tunnel token.

phases.objective: Add independent tunnel failover and certificate/health readback evidence for each hostname family without sharing Production and Dev credentials.
No DNS, Cloudflare, Hostinger, or external provider canary is executed by this source change.
Promote hostname-family routing to Production only through the protected Production branch and separately governed Hostinger/Cloudflare operations.
blockers: No Production DNS record, tunnel, certificate, or Hostinger setting is changed by this source change.
Production runtime verification must prove all three Production hostnames resolve to the intended Hostinger boundary before activation.
